headline: ChinaTalk and CSET examined fallout from Jensen Huang's resignation and threats to America's AI advantage, as Helen Toner warned we still can't trust AI CEOs and Wired flagged a new AI-fueled ransomware boom.

points.text: ChinaTalk held an emergency pod on 'Jensen Out, MATCH Act In?' to discuss the legislative fallout from Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO.
CSET warned that a convergence of political, commercial, and ideological pressures could undermine America's AI advantage, pointing to public controversies as a catalyst.
Axios described AI's 'four colliding crises' of trust, as Democrats surge to power and many Americans rebel against AI and data centers.
Helen Toner, the OpenAI board member who fired Sam Altman and now leads Georgetown's Center for Security and Emerging Technology, said in an interview that we still can't trust AI CEOs.
Wired warned of a new AI-fueled ransomware boom, noting that unsophisticated attackers are already using AI tools to cause serious damage.
Wired examined AI's rapid arrival in aviation amid shortages of pilots and air traffic controllers.
